sections.title: Ten blockers to clear before release
Every feature, and where it stands

overview.intro:
Deco Blocks is the next major version of Deco's framework, which ships today as the @decocms 7.x packages. The API in these docs is proposed and hasn't shipped yet; this page is the to-do list for releasing it (a release of the framework, not to be confused with content releases). To build it, we checked the proposed API feature by feature against three real sites that will move to it: a TanStack storefront on the current packages, a TanStack blog on an older package, and a Next.js storefront on another CMS.

No site can move using only what these docs describe. Each first needs something missing: Studio support, a way for blocks to read the current request, or SDK functions beyond the CMS. The ten release blockers gate the release; the status of every feature the three sites use is under Release readiness.
overview.readiness_lead: None of the 111 features those sites use is done yet: 11 are still to build, 66 are to finish, 28 are left to site code, and 6 go away with the migration.
overview.fix_docs: Fix the docs A few statements in these docs are still loose or wrong. The fixes are the first two docs work items: {{item:roadmap-docs--resolve-contradictions-in-these-docs}} and {{item:roadmap-docs--correct-studio-compatibility}}.

blockers.title: Let Studio talk to a next-major site
blockers.today: Studio reads the schema and content from the running site (/live/_meta, /.decofile) and calls it for previews, /deco/invoke and the secrets encrypt action. A next-major site serves none of these.
blockers.plan: Studio talks to stored content through the content protocol instead, which needs only the committed schema and .deco/content: Studio's GitHub backend in production, deco serve on a developer's machine. Features that need the site's code degrade in this version (see Studio and the content protocol).

blockers.title: Make the CLI write a schema Studio can read
blockers.today: The CLI writes .deco/schema.gen.json with top-level definitions; Studio reads .deco/meta.gen.json in LiveMeta shape (btoa keys, schema.root). There are no apps or actions groups, no per-type variant definitions, and the widget vocabulary is undocumented, so 22 image pickers would become text inputs and HTML fields plain strings.
blockers.plan: Emit Studio's exact format as .deco/schema.gen.json, one multivariate definition per field type a variant can fill, write static option lists into the schema, publish the JSDoc/@format table, and keep widget-alias detection and return-type loader unions.

blockers.title: Give blocks the page URL and route params
blockers.today: On SPA navigation getRequest() returns the /_serverFn URL, Next's headers() has no URL, app packages' loaders have no standard way to receive the URL or match.params, and apps-vtex's RequestContext is never populated.
blockers.plan: Add one binding-owned request scope (url, params, request, client, response headers) that both bindings' openPage populate and that block functions and site code can read, passing what a client needs as arguments.

blockers.title: Make draft preview work inside Studio's iframe
blockers.today: The SameSite=Lax cookie is rejected cross-site, the TanStack guide never sets it, and ?__draft=off is ignored. There's no no-store rule, and no StudioBridge or data-manifest-key, so click-to-select is lost.
blockers.plan: Ship withDeco()/decoProxy(), which set the cookie as Secure; SameSite=None; Partitioned, treat off/empty as exit and mark drafts private/no-store. Add <StudioBridge/>, and have <BlockList> emit Studio's section[data-manifest-key] marker.

blockers.title: Define the non-CMS SDK surface
blockers.today: apps-* and the ClickHouse telemetry depend on sdk/requestContext, instrumentedFetch, fetchCache and cachedLoader, and sites' widgets on sdk/useDevice and the Image and JsonLd hooks. These docs only list 'loaders, client, resolution, router'.
blockers.plan: The framework doesn't fetch data: the apps become thin, instrumented API clients over the framework's instrumented fetch, the core drops /deco/invoke and cachedLoader, and caching moves to the bindings. Publish a 7.x-to-next surface map and ship @decocms/blocks/image.
blockers.delivered_note: No work item covers the 7.x-to-next surface map yet.

blockers.title: Add a revision handle, an edge cache kit and an ISR recipe
blockers.today: Clients expose no revision and there's no forRevision. Degraded pages get cached. The planned check for a new release runs once a minute, at an idle moment (inside ctx.waitUntil on Workers), so a publish is live everywhere within seconds; a cold isolate serves the content module it was deployed with until its first check.
blockers.plan: Add a revision handle, a way to read and pin the revision a client serves (client.revision(), cms.forRevision(), onUpdate), and markDegraded(). Add an edge cache kit, withEdgeCache() in @decocms/tanstack, for caching rendered pages at the edge, and an ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration: re-rendering cached pages in the background) recipe for Next.js.

blockers.title: Stop resolving everything eagerly
blockers.today: The one registry rule resolves inputs bottom-up. Lazy defers nothing (43 wrappers on the storefront), hidden variants still run their loaders, and Resolved<T> can't be expressed.
blockers.plan: Add one deferral API: a Deferred<T> input type bound to the client's revision, which <BlockList> renders lazily. A multivariate over Deferred values resolves only the winner.

blockers.title: Make the next major load and resolve legacy content
blockers.today: Filename decoding is unspecified, and the alias bridge covers only pages, matchers and multivariate, while Studio writes Lazy, SeoV2, site/apps/site.ts, redirect, secret and the multi matcher. UNKNOWN_BLOCK now fails the parent block.
blockers.plan: Use the protocol's one filename rule (decode exactly once), widen the alias bridge, ship deco content (with deco schema reporting collisions), and have the CLI emit a runtime alias table.

blockers.title: Make routing accept the content sites already store
blockers.today: There's no splat, so /* PLPs never match. matchRoute throws per request on an ambiguity a single Studio commit can introduce. Page.seo is required but content stores null, and with no 404 gate unknown URLs return soft 200s.
blockers.plan: Add a trailing splat and make matchRoute non-throwing, with release-time validation. Make seo optional and add a critical-block notFound/redirect sentinel.

blockers.title: Define a model for apps, config and secrets
blockers.today: App loaders get no config, there's no apps manifest group, website/loaders/secret.ts can't decrypt, and Studio encrypts Secret fields through an action the site serves.
blockers.plan: Define the client contract (a factory that takes its config from site code), keep @decocms/blocks/secrets for decrypting existing secret entries, clients take their config from site code, and vendored loaders keep their old type names as aliases. No apps group in this version. Studio shows secret fields read-only in this version.

studio_new.title: Give Studio a schema it can read, so the editor loads
studio_new.today: Studio reads .deco/meta.gen.json or /live/_meta in LiveMeta shape, so a next-major site shows 'live meta unavailable'. On protocol projects it reads the committed .deco/schema.gen.json, which must be in that shape.

studio_new.title: Replace gallery, theme and in-place previews
studio_new.today: Studio's section thumbnails (its legacy name for block previews), global and theme previews, and Fast Preview in-place render all go through /live/previews, which runs site code. The protocol never does: these become name cards, or open the real page.

studio_new.title: Show Secret fields read-only on next-major sites
studio_new.today: Studio encrypts Secret fields through an encrypt action the site serves. Protocol projects have no such action, so secret and @format password fields are read-only in this version, and credentials live in environment variables.

studio_new.title: Fall back for @options, Run and pickers
studio_new.today: These need /deco/invoke and /live/invoke, which the protocol replaces. The blog ProductShelf picker even calls production's /deco/invoke with legacy VTEX keys. Pickers fall back to the schema's options, else free text; Run is hidden.

studio_new.title: Restore click-to-select
studio_new.today: There's no editor::inject listener, and the guides' renderers emit no Studio section[data-manifest-key] marker.

studio_new.title: Keep the draft past the first in-frame click
studio_new.today: The Lax cookie isn't stored cross-site and the TanStack guide never sets it. ?__draft=off can leave a stale draft behind.

studio_new.title: Give field-level variants a schema contract
studio_new.today: Studio's field variant UI needs a single-option block-ref whose definition has variants, and takes the inner field from variants.items.properties.value, else a plain string (schema-form.tsx:76-87, 254-280). The proposed API's one generic multivariate<T> gives the CLI no concrete T, so it has to take T from the field the variant fills. Legacy schemas had one flag per kind, e.g. website/flags/multivariate/image.ts.

studio_new.title: Keep variant tabs and the device toggle working
studio_new.today: x-deco-matchers-override and ?deviceHint have no reader in an app-owned multivariate.

studio_new.title: Stop Studio reading short type names as saved entries
studio_new.today: Studio classifies keys by file extension, so a site's UI blocks must keep legacy site/sections/X.tsx keys until it does a manifest lookup.

studio_new.title: Prevent entry names from colliding with types
studio_new.today: Studio's only write guard rejects keys with a source-file extension (block-key.ts:48-50). An editor can save an entry named hero, seo or page; under the proposed API's { ...savedEntries, ...blocks } the function wins and the entry is silently ignored. Only deco schema in CI catches it, after the commit is on the production branch.

studio_new.title: Let Studio see and edit flat redirect entries
studio_new.today: The Redirects collection lists only blocks typed exactly website/loaders/redirect.ts and writes { redirect: { from, to, type, discardQueryParameters } }, with temporary = 307 (redirect-data.ts:14,29-32,77). Flat redirect entries written by developers or agents never appear there and can't be edited.

studio_new.title: Edit local files from Studio; show local edits in dev
studio_new.today: The dev server serves neither endpoint Studio's local and tunnel modes use. With a site and token in .dev.vars, remoteLoader swaps in the production release over local edits.

studio_new.title: Speed up publishes and make failures visible
studio_new.today: The planned once-a-minute check makes a publish live within seconds, but nothing tells the editor when it is live. A failed forDraft silently shows published content.

studio_new.title: Keep experiments working on next-major sites
studio_new.today: Results are keyed on the random matcher's saved-entry name, which a pure block function never sees.

studio_legacy.title: Handle the legacy types Studio keeps writing
studio_legacy.today: website/pages/Page.tsx, SeoV2 on every new page, Rendering/Lazy.tsx (the ⚡ toggle), flags/multivariate/section.ts (hide), nested website/loaders/redirect.ts, website/loaders/secret.ts, site/apps/site.ts, the multi matcher, Theme. The bridge only aliases pages, matchers and multivariate, so these Studio actions produce UNKNOWN_BLOCK unless each site registers them.

studio_legacy.title: Stop hidden blocks from running
studio_legacy.today: 'Every variant resolves': a block hidden with a never-rule still runs its loaders, and its undefined renders 'temporarily unavailable'.

studio_legacy.title: Drop hidden array items instead of leaving holes
studio_legacy.today: Studio hides a banner or link by wrapping it in website/flags/multivariate.ts with a never rule (array-item-hidden.ts:35-40). Today's resolver drops undefined array items (resolve.ts:849-860). The proposed API's rule and resolve(page.sections) ('An array of results, one per block in the list') keep them, so components receive undefined entries.

studio_legacy.title: Fix the default-variant rule that makes other variants unreachable
studio_legacy.today: Studio seeds every new variant with an always rule (section-types.ts:26; a new field variant starts as two) and keeps the first always, else the last variant (section-variants.ts:158-168). These docs say 'put the always() variant first as the default' and 'first match wins', which makes every other variant unreachable; their own HomeHero puts always last.

studio_legacy.title: Decode filenames exactly once
studio_legacy.today: Studio writes encodeURIComponent(key). Real stems include pages-Category%2520Page-* and collections%2Fblog%2F*.

studio_legacy.title: Handle short-form pages in the page list and SEO
studio_legacy.today: page entries are missing from the page list and can be mistaken for the site-SEO owner.

studio_legacy.title: Stop keying the Blog tab on legacy names
studio_legacy.today: It looks for blog/loaders/*.ts and @decocms/apps-blog ≥ 7.53.0. The TanStack blog reads as unsupported-runtime today.

studio_legacy.title: Upgrade both TanStack sites so Studio can frame them
studio_legacy.today: Both TanStack sites send X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and lack ?__draft, so both plans start with an upgrade to the latest 7.x, past #390 (7.20.10) and #442 (7.34.0).

studio_legacy.title: Make content drift visible to editors
studio_legacy.today: Fields missing from the schema are hidden, and defaults apply only on save. The storefront's Header children are typed string[] today.

work_items.title: Add a request scope
work_items.plan: One binding-owned scope in @decocms/blocks, behind conditional exports: requestScope() returns { url, params, request, client, device, forcedRules }, plus appendResponseHeader(). Both bindings' openPage populate it with the real page href (port derivePageUrl), match.params and the per-request client. It replaces sdk/requestContext, the page-scope helpers and currentClient(), so apps import one framework-neutral port and content-reading loaders stay revision-pinned. device honors ?deviceHint and forcedRules exposes x-deco-matchers-override, both on drafts only.

work_items.title: Publish the content protocol and its package
work_items.plan: Write down the protocol between Studio and stored content: JSON-RPC 2.0 over one HTTP endpoint (POST /rpc, batches allowed) with four methods, describe, schema.get, blocks.list and blocks.apply, plus its errors, limits and conditional reads for polling. Ship it as @decocms/blocks-protocol (proposed name): the types and method definitions, a client, a server core over a ContentStorage interface, a filesystem storage and a black-box conformance suite any implementation runs over HTTP. Its key module holds the one filename rule (decode exactly once) that Studio, deco serve and deco content all import. See Studio compatibility.

work_items.title: Let Studio follow the deployed schema
work_items.plan: Studio builds its forms from whichever schema the user points it at, usually the one committed on the main branch. An option to follow the schema of the commit the production site runs would keep editors from adding a block type before the code that defines it is live. Update Schema generation once it ships.

work_items.title: Add a block renderer and a deferral API
work_items.plan: <BlockList> per binding: per-block Suspense, error boundary, clientOnly, sized fallbacks, eager above the fold, SEO routing, and Studio's section[data-manifest-key] frame on every block. One deferral API: a Deferred<T> input type passes a ref bound to the client's revision instead of resolving it. <BlockList> renders the ref lazily, and a multivariate whose values are Deferred<T> resolves only the winning variant.

work_items.title: Ship the withDeco() and decoProxy() entry wrappers
work_items.plan: withDeco(handler, { cms }) (TanStack) and decoProxy() (Next) own the per-request plumbing. They set the draft cookie as Secure; SameSite=None; Partitioned; HttpOnly and treat __draft=off or an empty value as exit. Drafted responses are private/no-store/noindex, and security headers carry frame-ancestors from an exported STUDIO_FRAME_ANCESTORS, never X-Frame-Options. Studio routes are optional. The CMS keys draft caches on the API ETag, bounded by an LRU.

work_items.title: Add a revision handle
work_items.plan: client.revision(), cms.forRevision(rev) / forRelease({ revision }), CMS.onUpdate(cb) and update({ force }).

work_items.title: Turn the apps into thin, instrumented clients
work_items.plan: The framework doesn't fetch data. Each companion app (VTEX, Shopify, Wake, Magento, Algolia, Resend, …) becomes a thin API client for its platform: typed request functions over the framework's instrumented fetch, keeping the platform's API and generated types. Latency is measured to the response headers, retries count as one data point with a retries attribute, and error logs are structured and never contain upstream bodies, tokens or cookies. The VTEX client keeps retry and circuit breaking on by default. Converters to commerce types, the cart, user and wishlist hooks, cart, session and auth flows, and website features beyond the three built-in matchers (SEO helpers, sitemaps, redirect logic, analytics scripts) move to platform templates and site code. Upstream API clients has the recipe for writing a client.

work_items.title: Remove /deco/invoke and cachedLoader
work_items.plan: The core drops the /deco/invoke endpoint and cachedLoader. Per-shopper reads and actions become the framework's own server functions or route handlers, which call the clients directly. A block function may still fetch data when a site wants it to; it calls a client like any other code.

work_items.title: Cache upstream requests in the bindings
work_items.plan: Caching depends on the platform, so it lives in the framework bindings, not in the clients: the Cloudflare Cache API in @decocms/tanstack on Workers, Next's data cache in @decocms/nextjs. The instrumented fetch reports whether each response came from the cache (the cached label), and drafts bypass the cache.

work_items.title: Add remoteLoader options
work_items.plan: { interval, coldStartTimeoutMs, channel, onUpdate, onError }, also accepted by createCMS. interval is in milliseconds, defaults to DECO_CONTENT_INTERVAL or 60 000, and has a 60 000 minimum (lower values are raised to one minute with a warning). Each check runs one interval ± 10 s after the previous one and fetches only the revision hash. The SDK schedules due checks itself at an idle moment: requestIdleCallback, then scheduler.postTask, then setTimeout; an unref'd timer on Node; and after the response inside ctx.waitUntil on Workers. Instances are process-wide singletons keyed by configuration, with a resetForTests() helper.

work_items.title: Document and support KV-only content for large Workers sites
work_items.plan: With content plus site and token, the bundled content module stays in memory as the fallback next to the live release, against a Worker isolate's 128 MB limit, and it also counts toward the script size limit. Document passing a KV-backed Loader as content for large sites, so no copy is bundled and the fallback is read from KV only when needed. Ship a first-party kvLoader(env.CONTENT, { key }), and a documented deploy step that writes the content to the key before the new Worker takes traffic, since with a missing key every new isolate fails its first reads until its first release check.

work_items.title: Add session, region, delivery promise and prices to apps-vtex
work_items.plan: Typed requests for delivery promise in Intelligent Search, tax-inclusive prices, full installments with InterestRate, Intelligent Search events, and createVtexIoClient for persisted IO queries. The session module (resolveRegion, setSegment), the session and cart hooks move to the VTEX platform template, which sites copy.

work_items.title: Add a Studio bridge
work_items.plan: A client-safe <StudioBridge /> that accepts editor::inject only from an explicit list of Studio origins, configurable for self-hosted and native Studio. Also resolve(t, { withType: true }) to recover the block type.

work_items.title: Ship an SEO kit in the platform templates
work_items.plan: SEO helpers are website features, so they live in the platform templates, as code a site owns: PageSeo and SEO functions pre-aliased to SeoV2/Seo/SeoPDPV2/SeoPLPV2, mergeSiteSeo(siteSeo, pageSeo) as the one site-SEO merge (sharing a test suite with Studio), seoToNextMetadata / seoToTanStackHead, JSON-LD builders and a <JsonLd> renderer.

work_items.title: Define the client contract
work_items.plan: Each client package exports a factory that takes its configuration as arguments (for example createVtexClient({ account, appKey, appToken }), read from environment variables in site code) and typed request functions. No block map, no @decocms/tanstack dependency, no dynamic module import. Installing an app from Studio's store is unavailable on next-major sites: a client is added in code.

work_items.title: Add an edge cache kit
work_items.plan: withEdgeCache(entry, { segment, profiles }) in @decocms/tanstack, keyed by URL, build, revision and segment. It skips drafts, cold-start fallback and degraded pages. Plus cacheHeaders(profile) and markDegraded().

work_items.title: Define a per-client memoization contract
work_items.plan: A saved entry, or an identical inline block, resolves once per client (keyed by type plus canonical inputs), and concurrent calls share in-flight promises.

work_items.title: Add a splat to matchRoute and stop request-time throws
work_items.plan: A trailing /* or /:rest* at lowest precedence (also for Redirect.from, with substitution), a deterministic tie-break that returns a Result, and case-insensitive matching as an option.

work_items.title: Ship @decocms/blocks/secrets
work_items.plan: @decocms/blocks/secrets: a secret block aliased as website/loaders/secret.ts that decrypts existing encrypted values with DECO_CRYPTO_KEY, so content saved by today's Studio keeps working. New credentials go in environment variables. Studio shows secret and @format password fields read-only in this version, so there's no encrypt action to serve. Amend 'the token is the only secret' in Preview.

work_items.title: Add a site-wide layout helper
work_items.plan: mergeGlobals(site, page), with layout blocks resolved on the page's client. Site SEO defaults go through the SEO kit's mergeSiteSeo.

work_items.title: Keep the TanStack router helpers available
work_items.plan: Keep createDecoRouter, or export decoParseSearch/decoStringifySearch and the CSP-nonce wiring.

work_items.title: Add an image module
work_items.plan: @decocms/blocks/image (optimized URLs, srcset, Studio quality params), a Next loaderFile, and TanStack <Image>/<Picture>. Export the widget aliases.

work_items.title: Support experiments; move the analytics bootstrap to the templates
work_items.plan: Analytics scripts are a website feature: the DECO.events bootstrap and a typed useSendEvent/dispatch move to the platform templates. The framework keeps what experiments need: an assignExperiments() middleware helper and a way for random matchers to know their entry name. Variant exposure events for real-user monitoring come after the first release (see {{item:roadmap-later--add-real-user-monitoring}}).

work_items.title: Add a not-found and redirect gate before streaming
work_items.plan: A critical block (or seo) may return { notFound } or { redirect }, which the app maps to notFound()/redirect(). Framework control-flow errors are rethrown.

work_items.title: Report inbound requests and edge cache hits from the bindings
work_items.plan: Both bindings report inbound request metrics and edge cache hits into the hosted Deco CMS's telemetry pipeline, outside createDecoWorkerEntry on TanStack and with a meter bootstrap on Node and Next.js. Telemetry is hosted-only: without a site ID and token nothing is sent, and the framework adds no export hook of its own; apps that want their own observability instrument their code with OpenTelemetry as usual.

work_items.title: Add the Telemetry block, sampling and aggregation
work_items.plan: createCMS({ blocks, content, site, token }): the site ID and site token (usually DECO_SITE and DECO_SITE_TOKEN) load hosted content and send telemetry; without both, nothing is sent. Telemetry settings (on or off, sample rates) live in a well-known saved entry, Telemetry, whose schema the framework provides: a committed .deco/content/Telemetry.json that deco content scaffolds. Editors change it in Studio, which commits it through its GitHub integration like any content edit; it travels with every release and running servers pick it up with their next content check; without it, the framework's defaults apply. Error logs are sampled; metrics are aggregated in memory before they're sent.

work_items.title: Rename apps-salesforce to a Marketing Cloud Personalization client
work_items.plan: The package is a client for Salesforce Marketing Cloud Personalization (formerly Evergage), so name it for that, on the same thin-client model as the other apps.

work_items.title: Add predictive search and shipping rates to apps-shopify
work_items.plan: A predictive-search suggestions loader and a shipping-rates helper.

work_items.title: Put sitemap generation in the platform templates
work_items.plan: Sitemaps are a website feature, so the templates ship them as site code: sitemapEntries(client, { types, expand, exclude }), toSitemapXml/toSitemapIndex, plus a Shopify sitemap merge.

work_items.title: Give the traffic split a home and bypass drafts by default
work_items.plan: Move withABTesting to @decocms/tanstack/traffic-split and bypass drafts by default.

work_items.title: Write a Studio-compatible schema file
work_items.plan: Write .deco/schema.gen.json in Studio's format (deco-meta@1, byte-compatible with today's meta.gen.json, which the protocol still reads as a fallback): manifest.blocks, schema.definitions keyed by padded, path-independent btoa, and schema.root unions. Add apps and actions groups. For every field a variant can fill (a field of type T), emit a monomorphized multivariate definition per T (value typed as T) under Studio's legacy per-kind keys (website/flags/multivariate/section.ts, …/image.ts, …), so the field variant UI renders the right input.

work_items.title: Write static option lists into the schema
work_items.plan: Studio no longer calls the site for picker options, so deco schema writes every static list into the schema as an enum: string-literal unions, TypeScript enums and @options literal lists, with labels where the code gives them. A picker whose options come from a function falls back to free text in this version.

work_items.title: Widen the legacy alias bridge
work_items.plan: Alias Lazy/SingleDeferred/Deferred, Seo*, site/apps/site.ts, resolved, requestToParam, secret, redirect (with shape mapping), the device and random matchers, the multi matcher (website/matchers/multi.ts and $live/matchers/MatchMulti.ts, whose and/or combinators keep the { op, matchers } shape that Studio's variant calendar and rule labels read), Analytics and Theme, and list exactly which paths.

work_items.title: Add validation commands to the CLI
work_items.plan: Content-model checks in deco schema reporting UNKNOWN_BLOCK, NOT_FOUND, orphans, schema violations and route collisions, with an optional resolve-every-page smoke test.

work_items.title: Add deco schema --check, a compatibility check
work_items.plan: deco schema --check <base> generates the schema, compares it with a base .deco/schema.gen.json (in CI, the one on the target branch), lists every breaking change and exits non-zero if there is one. It writes nothing. Breaking: removing a block type (any removal, since it compares schemas only), removing or renaming a field, adding a required field or making an optional one required, and narrowing a field's type (a string becoming a union of allowed values, a union losing a member, a tighter limit: a lower @maximum/@maxLength or a higher @minimum/@minLength). Not breaking: adding a type, adding an optional field, widening a type. An alias keeps a renamed type's old name in the schema, so a block type renamed with an alias passes. The docs ship a GitHub Actions example. Compatibility is checked here, before merge; the Deco API and remoteLoader don't compare schemas at runtime. Ships with the first release.

work_items.title: Publish the tag and widget vocabulary
work_items.plan: A full JSDoc/@format table (image-uri, video-uri, html, rich-text, rich-text-inline, textarea, markdown, color-input, icon-select, @titleBy, @hide, @options, @label, @minItems…), with widget-alias detection kept, labelled literals, and a golden test against generate-schema.ts.

work_items.title: Ship migration codemods
work_items.plan: deco migrate block-map from 7.x manifests, one 7 → next import codemod (6.x sites upgrade to 7.x first), an SEO-hoist rule, APP_REGISTRY → block maps and a requestToParam scaffold.

work_items.title: Vendor the loaders and actions a site uses during migration
work_items.plan: The companion apps stop shipping loaders and actions, so the migration copies the ones a site actually uses (found from its saved content and imports) into the site's own code, rewritten over the thin clients, with their legacy type names kept as aliases so saved content still resolves.

work_items.title: Build a FastStore importer
work_items.plan: deco import faststore: VTEX Headless CMS content becomes .deco/content with $componentKey rewritten to path-shaped keys, content types become page entries, and JSONC becomes TS scaffolds.

work_items.title: Match fields to block functions by return type
work_items.plan: A field's type is the value the function receives. deco schema reads each block function's awaited return type, so an object field of type T accepts a plain T or any block whose function returns T or Promise<T> (anyOf $refs), and Studio's block picker offers those functions plus the saved blocks that resolve through them. ReactNode and ReactNode[] fields take only functions that return JSX (a React element, or a promise of one; Studio's legacy __SECTION_REF__): ReactNode also includes strings, numbers and booleans, but functions returning those are left out, so matchers never fit sections. Simple types (string, number, boolean, literal unions) stay plain inputs. The generic multivariate<T> fits any field, with T taken from the field and its undefined (no rule matched) allowed, and functions that return boolean fill a variant's rule. The CLI follows imported app maps with last-key-wins and warns on any.

work_items.title: Add a singleton tag and a descriptor type
work_items.plan: A @singleton JSDoc tag marks a block type saved once per site, such as site-wide settings, so Studio opens its one entry instead of a list. A Descriptor<P> type gives data-mode blocks, which return descriptors instead of JSX, one shared return type, so the CLI can match them to fields the way it matches JSX. Hiding blocks from pickers (the old @catalog false plan) waits until categories of blocks are designed.

work_items.title: Specify the filename rule and ship a content bundle
work_items.plan: Use the protocol package's one filename rule: a file name is decoded exactly once, and Studio, deco serve and deco content import the same module, with a collision report. deco content writes .deco/content.gen.ts, one import per JSON file, exporting the snapshot { revision, blocks } with the revision computed the same way the Deco API computes it, and computeRevision is exported.

work_items.title: Emit a runtime alias table
work_items.plan: The CLI emits an alias table, a list of second names for types. createCMS accepts it, so list() and resolve() work through aliases. The schema carries it too, mapping the short names (page, redirect, always, never, multivariate, secret) to the well-known types Studio's special screens look for, so those screens keep working for renamed types.

work_items.title: Ship deco serve, a local server for Studio
work_items.plan: A command of the deco CLI in @decocms/blocks, deco serve, that serves the content protocol on localhost:<port> for the developer's working tree (the app root from --root, or the nearest folder with a .deco/, which it reports to Studio in describe), so Studio can edit the files on the developer's machine: the saved content in .deco/content, the schema in .deco/schema.gen.json (read-only) and the upload URLs for assets. It listens on the loopback address by default, prints a bearer token and a connect link at start, allows only Studio's origins (CORS) and answers Chrome's local-network permission preflight. Writes land in .deco/content and the app hot-reloads; the server regenerates the content module when a write adds or removes a file. It never commits. deco schema --watch and deco content --watch stay as they are.

work_items.title: Store uploads in the repository with deco serve
work_items.plan: Without the hosted Deco CMS, files uploaded in Studio are written into the repository: deco serve accepts them at PUT /assets/<name> beside /rpc, with the same token, origin and Host checks, writes them to .deco/assets/ (or the folder --assets <dir> names, such as public/assets), never overwrites an existing file, and answers with the path Studio stores in the field, always /assets/<name>, such as /assets/summer-banner.jpg. The folder is relative to the folder that contains .deco. describe reports the folder and the largest file accepted in its assets field, which is null with --read-only, and uploads are then refused. The site serves the folder as static files at /assets/; public/assets needs no setup.

work_items.title: Ship the deco command
work_items.plan: These docs run npx @decocms/blocks schema, but @decocms/blocks doesn't declare a deco bin yet. Ship the CLI inside @decocms/blocks, so Quickstart installs one package and the CLI always matches the runtime version. Declare deco as the package's single bin, so npx @decocms/blocks <command> runs it with nothing installed and package.json scripts call deco <command>; the bin is a small JavaScript file that loads the TypeScript sources, so it runs under plain Node as well as Bun. Export the commands from the @decocms/blocks/cli subpath, make typescript a required peer dependency (so npm and Bun install it) that the CLI loads only when a command runs, and keep the runtime from ever importing the cli subpath, so app bundles never include the CLI. It has three commands, deco schema [--root <dir>] [--watch] [--check <base>], deco content [--root <dir>] [--watch] and deco serve [--root <dir>] [--port <n>] [--host <addr>] [--app-url <url>] [--token <t>] [--allow-origin <origin>]… [--assets <dir>] [--read-only]. Every command works on one folder, .deco/, in the app root (the folder with the app's package.json). --root is the folder that contains it; by default, every command walks up from the current folder to the first folder with a .deco/. There are no input or output paths: deco schema reads .deco/blocks.ts (or .deco/blocks.tsx) and writes .deco/schema.gen.json; deco content reads .deco/content and writes .deco/content.gen.ts, and never reads the block map. The .gen. infix marks the two generated files. The flags of each command are in the CLI reference.

work_items.title: Build Studio's GitHub content backend
work_items.plan: A ContentStorage inside Studio's API that reads and writes .deco/content through the GitHub API, in the folder the project's "app root" setting names (a monorepo subfolder included). Every write is a commit, and all files of one blocks.apply go in one tree and one commit, with file contents inlined in the tree request. Clients poll on window focus and about every 30 seconds with one batched conditional request. Publishing, the draft pointer and ?__draft= links stay Studio routes outside the protocol. Drop the requirement for a deployed preview URL, so a project with no deployment can still be edited.

work_items.title: Move Studio's editor onto the protocol client
work_items.plan: Projects with a committed .deco/schema.gen.json or .deco/meta.gen.json under their folder use the protocol client, so v7 projects that commit meta.gen.json qualify, and a project setting picks the path. Fresh and Deno sites, whose schema exists only at runtime, stay on the legacy path. Features that need the site's code degrade: block previews become name cards or open the real page (the local dev app, or the deployed site with a ?__draft= link), dynamic pickers fall back to the schema's options, else free text, secret and password fields are read-only, and Run and installing apps from the store are hidden. Autosave stays last-writer-wins. Add the connect flow for a local deco serve endpoint, with a one-line explainer before Chrome's local-network prompt.

work_items.title: Add a play workspace for local editing
work_items.plan: Let anyone edit the files on their machine in Studio without a Deco account: a connect link from deco serve opens a play workspace in Studio that talks only to that local server, with no site, team or sign-in. Hosted features (Studio's GitHub backend, releases, drafts on your site, hosted asset storage and telemetry) stay with a connected site.

work_items.title: Store uploads in Deco's asset storage
work_items.plan: With the hosted Deco CMS, Studio's GitHub backend sends uploads to Deco's asset storage (backed by Amazon S3) instead of the repository, and saves each file's CDN address in the field, so images are served from a CDN and the repository doesn't grow. A field can hold either a CDN address or a path to a file in the repository, so sites that started with local uploads keep working.

work_items.title: Fix the Add Section gate
work_items.plan: Studio shows Add Section only when a preview server is configured. Gate it on having the schema and the blocks instead; otherwise adding blocks to a page disappears on protocol projects.

work_items.title: Read manifest groups for pages, redirects, content and apps
work_items.plan: Support several page types, a content collection screen and singletons. Read flat redirect entries alongside the nested legacy shape, mapping type to permanent.

work_items.title: Use manifest lookup instead of path heuristics
work_items.plan: Replace the file-extension module-or-entry check and Studio's legacy "/sections/" path heuristics, and refuse to save an entry whose name is a manifest key.

work_items.title: Build the Deco API release service
work_items.plan: A release endpoint, site IDs and site tokens (with a DECO_SITE and DECO_SITE_TOKEN lifecycle), rejection of ambiguous-route releases, and per-environment channels. The service serves every commit as it lands and doesn't compare schemas; compatibility is checked in CI by deco schema --check.

work_items.title: Align the preview protocol
work_items.plan: Send an empty __draft= (or keep 'off' as a documented contract) and force variants in the draft content. On protocol projects the canvas opens the real page with the draft pointer, and gallery thumbnails and in-place renders are replaced by name cards, since the protocol never runs site code.

work_items.title: Drop legacy names from the Blog tab and experiments
work_items.plan: Detect the blog from the manifest, and stop keying experiments on the random matcher's entry name.

work_items.title: Label matchers from their schema and keep enum titles
work_items.plan: Label short-key matchers from their schema, dedupe aliased matchers, and keep oneOf const titles.

work_items.title: Add a per-page-type catalog and a page settings form
work_items.plan: Use the anyOf on a page type's sections list as Studio's catalog, and render the remaining page props as a form.

work_items.title: Bring Studio's SEO merge to parity with the kit
work_items.plan: Run Studio's mergeSeo (seo-editor.tsx) against the kit's mergeSiteSeo test suite, and decide whether descriptionTemplate applies.

work_items.title: Add a content-live signal
work_items.plan: Every response carries the served revision in x-deco-revision, and the CMS reports each revision it swaps in to the Deco API with the site token. Studio polls the API and shows a publish as pending until a report for its revision arrives, then live.

work_items.title: Build the telemetry collector
work_items.plan: An endpoint that accepts aggregated metrics and sampled error logs, authenticated by site ID and site token. Switching a site's telemetry off needs no special channel: Studio commits the change to the site's .deco/content/Telemetry.json through its GitHub integration, like any content edit, and running servers pick it up with their next content check.

work_items.title: Update the injected agent rules
work_items.plan: Replace the two wrong rules for next-major sites. Content edits go only in .deco/content/<encodeURIComponent(key)>.json. .deco/blocks.ts and .deco/content are the site's; two files are generated and never edited by hand: .deco/schema.gen.json, which deco schema rewrites after any change to a block's types, and .deco/content.gen.ts, which deco content writes and git ignores. A new type needs a block-map entry. remoteLoader picks up releases within seconds, not on save, and with DECO_SITE and DECO_SITE_TOKEN set the dev server serves the API release, not local edits.

work_items.title: Resolve contradictions in these docs
work_items.plan: Make Page.seo optional, drop array elements that resolve to undefined (Studio's hidden array items), make a hidden block's undefined render nothing, and fix the credential sentence in Preview.

work_items.title: Correct Studio compatibility
work_items.plan: Studio compatibility now describes the content protocol, with the old site endpoints (/live/_meta, /.decofile, /live/previews, /deco/invoke, /live/invoke) as the legacy path. Keep it in step with the protocol as Studio's implementation lands, and state that sites allow framing through frame-ancestors, never X-Frame-Options, as the entry wrappers do.

work_items.title: Fix the TanStack guides
work_items.plan: Mount withDeco() instead of hand-wiring the draft cookie. Add validateSearch/loaderDeps and staleTime, and state that getRequest() is the RPC request on SPA navigation, so the page URL comes from the request scope.

work_items.title: Write the recipes that gate cutover
work_items.plan: Write these before the first site migrates: site-wide content and layout (header, footer, theme), site settings, 404/500, route params in blocks, per-shopper reads and actions as server functions (invoke → server fn), and regionalization cache keys.

work_items.title: Write the post-cutover recipes
work_items.plan: Page-level data shared by a page's blocks, client data fetching, server-only upstream proxies, overriding an app's block, tabs over pre-resolved data, head tags from blocks, locale, and robots/static SEO files.

work_items.title: Write a FastStore-to-Blocks guide
work_items.plan: Decision: port @faststore/core's UI components (FastStore calls them sections) into the site as vendored code, with no separate storefront UI kit; the commerce hooks they need come from apps-vtex. The guide covers the choice of App Router or TanStack Start (there's no Pages Router path), a core-internals → apps-vtex map, a fragment → loader map and the override → composition recipe.

work_items.title: Fix the Next guide
work_items.plan: Mount decoProxy() instead of wiring the draft cookie by hand. Wrap client() in cache(), map the full PageSeo and degrade SEO errors instead of throwing, make release routes ISR/static, and cover transpilePackages and outputFileTracingIncludes.

work_items.title: Finish the operations page
work_items.plan: Telemetry now covers what's sent and sampling, and The hosted Deco CMS covers connecting a site. Still to add: (1) the DECO_SITE and DECO_SITE_TOKEN lifecycle (issue, rotate, scope) and a one-time warning when createCMS runs in production without them; (2) a per-host table of how the SDK schedules its once-a-minute check on Workers, Node and Vercel; (3) default bounds for every in-isolate cache and how to change them; (4) the 7.x → next env and binding table. Plus a CI job that resolves one block per app package in a Workers production build, to catch dynamic-import failures.

work_items.title: Add notes to the Rendering page
work_items.plan: Add four statements to Rendering. Inline <script> in a streamed boundary runs on parse, before the boundary is revealed, so use effects. <BlockList> keeps above-the-fold blocks eager, with sized skeletons below. UI stores (drawers, minicart) are app code, created per request. Request-scope values are read during resolve and passed as props, because AsyncLocalStorage is gone by the time a streamed boundary renders.

work_items.title: Fill in the schema reference details
work_items.plan: Unions to anyOf with const discriminators, intersections and recursion, type resolution through packages, filename-to-entry encoding, and how a variant on a field of type T becomes one multivariate definition per T.

work_items.title: Add real-user monitoring
work_items.plan: Real-user monitoring (RUM): what visitors experience in the browser, as a customer-facing alternative to Google Analytics, linked to A/B testing through variant exposure events. It's planned as a follow-up after the first release, not a release blocker, and it's being worked on. Its API isn't designed yet.

work_items.title: Detect conflicting edits in Studio
work_items.plan: Studio's autosave is last-writer-wins in the first version of the protocol. Send each save with ifMatch, the version the form opened with, and show 'changed elsewhere: reload or overwrite' when it conflicts.

work_items.title: Serve the content protocol from the dev server
work_items.plan: Let @decocms/tanstack/vite mount the content protocol's handler in the app's own dev server, so editing the files on your machine from Studio needs one process instead of two. deco serve stays for other setups.

work_items.title: Add long polling for faster local updates
work_items.plan: An optional wait on the protocol's conditional reads, announced in describe, so a hand edit in the working tree shows in Studio in a fraction of a second instead of on the next 2-second poll. One tab per endpoint would hold the request, so autosaves never queue behind it.

sites.name: TanStack storefront
sites.description: A storefront on TanStack Start and Cloudflare Workers, on the current @decocms 7.x packages.
sites.headline: Closest to the next major. Before it can move, the proposed API needs successors for the pieces it relies on today: the worker entry (the Workers request handler that wraps the app), the edge cache, the page-URL plumbing and the endpoints Studio calls.

steps.title: Fix dark metrics and /deco/invoke 404s
steps.text: createInstrumentedFetch("shopify") has no onComplete, so upstream metrics are dark. Site loaders called through /deco/invoke 404.

steps.title: Upgrade 7.20.7 to the latest 7.x
steps.text: The lockfile pins 7.20.7, which still sends X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and has no ?__draft binding. Moving past #390 (7.20.10) and #442 (7.34.0) lets Studio frame and preview the site today, and leaves one 7 → next step.

steps.title: Keep Studio's forms, previews and @options working after the move
steps.text: Next-major serves none of /live/_meta, /live/previews or /deco/invoke, and its schema file isn't what Studio reads. Forms, previews, @options fields and the Loaders tab all stop.

steps.title: Drop apps-shopify's @decocms/tanstack dependency and document its SDK imports
steps.text: It imports @decocms/blocks/sdk/{fetchTimeout,instrumentedFetch} and depends on @decocms/tanstack.

steps.title: Keep the edge cache and A/B split without createDecoWorkerEntry
steps.text: Workers Cache is on, with segment keys and degraded-page protection. The SITES_KV traffic split has no home.

steps.title: Keep the page URL on SPA navigation (PLP, search, PDP)
steps.text: Today's x-deco-page-url and derivePageUrl workarounds have no successor.

steps.title: Do the mechanical port
steps.text: Hand-write the block map (27 UI blocks, 12 loaders) with the path-shaped keys Studio needs, add the ~8-line requestToParam shim (app code), and replace Image/Picture (~20 files). The content fixes below register types into this map.

steps.title: Fix the content before cutover
steps.text: Rewrite the Category page path /* to /:collection, guard the PDP's seo: null and hoist SEO blocks out of sections[]. Register in the block map, or remove, ~20 unknown types, including the resolved built-in that Header.json's searchbar uses. Fix the Newsletter and Header drift, and hold MIGRATION_NEXT_STEPS' *Config Props regrouping until a content validator exists.

steps.title: Restore deferral and stop duplicate loads
steps.text: Its 43 Lazy wrappers (21 with inline loaders) lose deferral until Deferred<T> exists. 'PLP Loader' is referenced twice per page and needs the per-client memo.

sites.name: TanStack blog
sites.description: A blog on TanStack Start and Cloudflare Workers, on an older single-package version of the framework.
sites.headline: Simple content and a clean route tree, but it's on an older package: it upgrades to 7.x first (until then, Studio can't open it in its preview frame), and its Studio blog workflow depends on old loader names and apps-blog.

steps.title: Upgrade 6.12 to the latest 7.x first
steps.text: Fix upgrade-6-to-7 for the blog's specifiers (~45 symbols across 13 subpaths), then run it. That also drops X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and adds ?__draft, so Studio can frame the site. The move to next is then the same 7 → next step as the storefront's.

steps.title: Untie the Blog tab from legacy names and apps-blog
steps.text: It keys off blog/loaders/*.ts and @decocms/apps-blog ≥ 7.53.0, but the site is on @decocms/apps 5.2.0. Its meta sits at src/server/admin/meta.gen.json with Windows-path keys, and setInvokeLoaders exists only for Studio.

steps.title: Stop blog loaders reading the global decofile
steps.text: apps-blog's getRecordsByPath uses loadBlocks(), so under a pure CMS drafts read the wrong revision. It needs the request scope's client, or the lookups move to route code.

steps.title: Keep the live publish path
steps.text: regen-blocks.yml (Studio publish, then a regen commit, then a Workers Build) is how content ships today. Keep it until the release service and remoteLoader exist.

steps.title: Return real 404s for unknown URLs and stop routing /404 publicly
steps.text: The 7 pages form a valid trie, but unknown URLs are soft 200s via /:slug and /404 is publicly routable.

steps.title: Alias legacy types and render body blocks
steps.text: 25 legacy types (210 occurrences) need aliases, and body blocks become a data-only block with a renderer.

steps.title: Handle images, the edge profile and app config
steps.text: The blog uses plain <img>, no edge profile fits posts, and app config goes through apps-blog.

steps.title: Two current bugs go away with the migration
steps.text: One is in the layout cache, the other in the build-time site-globals snapshot, which never reaches draft preview. The migration replaces both.

sites.name: Next.js storefront
sites.description: A Next.js storefront on another CMS. Not on Deco today, so this is a re-platform, not an upgrade.
sites.headline: A re-platform, not an upgrade. The target framework, the content, FastStore's native sections and the session model all come before the missing pieces in the proposed API even come into play.

steps.title: Pick the target framework and move to it
steps.text: Pick the target first: the App Router (the only guide; the Pages Router has none) or TanStack Start. It decides how FastStore's native sections get rebuilt. Its code imports @faststore/core internals, and most of its hook files, and the files that use its translation hook, lack "use client".

steps.title: Bring the content in from VTEX Headless CMS
steps.text: The content lives in VTEX Headless CMS. There's no Headless CMS-to-.deco/content importer, the JSONC schemas must become TS types, and per-page-type whitelists of allowed blocks and singletons have no TS or Studio expression.

steps.title: Rebuild what @faststore/core renders
steps.text: Its native sections (FastStore's UI components), including the stateful cart, search and session ones, the global ones (header, footer) and the 404/500 pages. No UI kit exists.

steps.title: Give apps-vtex session, region and delivery promise
steps.text: Without a populated request scope, regionalized Intelligent Search queries also silently fall back to the default region.

steps.title: Rewrite the data shapes to schema.org
steps.text: FastStore GraphQL moves to apps-commerce schema.org: the PDP view model, the product card, the BFF fields, tax prices and installments.

steps.title: Port client state and the core patches
steps.text: The useSearch state machine and the client fetches become server functions. The behaviours the core patches add are re-created as app code.

steps.title: Rename $componentKey values to path-shaped keys and avoid type-name collisions
steps.text: There's no legacy Deco content, so no legacy-type aliases. The importer must still rename $componentKey values (Navbar, Footer, Alert…) to path-shaped keys until Studio does manifest lookups, and avoid entry names that collide with type names. The content protocol and schema fixes ({{item:roadmap-api--publish-the-content-protocol-and-its-package}}, {{item:roadmap-cli--write-a-studio-compatible-schema-file}}) gate editing.
